additions.title: R (Ayinde) v London Borough of Haringey; Al-Haroun v Qatar National Bank QPSC [2025] EWHC 1383 (Admin)
additions.publisher: High Court of Justice, King's Bench Division, Divisional Court (The National Archives, Find Case Law)
additions.quote: measures must now be taken by those within the legal profession with individual leadership responsibilities (such as heads of chambers and managing partners)
additions.why: A Divisional Court judgment, after lawyers put fictitious AI-generated citations before the court, saying that those who lead legal practices must take practical and effective measures so that everyone understands their duties when using AI, and that courts will ask whether they did. The clearest UK judicial statement that rules on AI use are a leadership responsibility. Addressed to the legal profession in England and Wales; it does not prescribe a written policy by name.

additions.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), Article 17: Quality management system
additions.publisher: European Commission, AI Act Service Desk
additions.quote: That system shall be documented in a systematic and orderly manner in the form of written policies, procedures and instructions
additions.why: The binding EU rule that comes closest to requiring an AI policy set: providers of high-risk systems must document their quality management system as written policies, procedures and instructions, including an accountability framework. The Commission's copy of the consolidated text (stated as at 27 July 2026), not the Official Journal. Applies to providers of high-risk systems only, so it reaches UK firms only where they place such systems on the EU market; no application date is given here.

additions.title: Data protection audit framework, Accountability toolkit: Policies and procedures
additions.locator: Second control measure (review and approval process), list 'Ways to meet our expectations'; first control measure, 'Options to consider'
additions.quote: Update policies and procedures without undue delay when they require changes, eg because of operational change, court or regulatory decisions or changes in regulatory guidance.
additions.why: What the regulator's auditors test in a policy set: endorsed at the highest level of management, approved by a senior person, reviewed on documented dates, updated on legal or operational change, and backed by a mechanism to show staff have read it. It maps closely onto the levels of this criterion. Carries the 'under review' banner following the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025; the page shows no publication date, so the year is the year read. Data protection only, not AI governance in general.

additions.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile, NIST AI 600-1
additions.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
additions.locator: Suggested action GV-1.4-002 (under GOVERN 1.4), printed p.15 (PDF p.19); see also GV-3.2-003 and GV-6.1-010
additions.quote: Establish transparent acceptable use policies for GAI that address illegal use or applications of GAI.
additions.why: A free standard, dated 2024, that turns the framework's general policy outcome into specific actions on acceptable-use policies for generative AI, including extending them to contractors and third-party tools. Voluntary, US, and limited to generative AI.

additions.title: Principles alone cannot guarantee ethical AI
additions.publisher: Brent Mittelstadt (arXiv; published in Nature Machine Intelligence)
additions.quote: (3) proven methods to translate principles into practice, and (4) robust legal and professional accountability mechanisms
additions.why: Peer-reviewed argument that statements of principle do little by themselves because AI development lacks tested ways to turn them into practice and lacks accountability mechanisms. The case for policies that carry owners, procedures and monitoring. Author's arXiv copy (version 2, February 2020) of the article in Nature Machine Intelligence 1, 501-507; the journal copy was not read. Conceptual, not empirical.

additions.title: The Ethics of AI Ethics: An Evaluation of Guidelines
additions.publisher: Thilo Hagendorff (arXiv; published in Minds and Machines)
additions.quote: effectiveness of guidelines or ethical codes is almost zero and that they do not change the behavior of professionals from the tech community
additions.why: Review of 21 major AI ethics guidelines (the count in this version) which reports a controlled study (McNamara and others, 2018; 63 students and 105 professional developers) finding that showing people a code of ethics made no significant difference to their decisions. Evidence that an unread or unenforced policy changes nothing, which is why adherence has to be measured. Author's arXiv copy (version 2) of the article in Minds and Machines (2020); the journal copy could not be read. The study it reports is a single vignette experiment on software engineers, cited here second-hand.

rejected.title: Springer journal copies (AI & Society, Philosophy & Technology, AI and Ethics, Minds and Machines)
rejected.reason: Blocked: link.springer.com returned a 'Client Challenge' page to every request (four articles tried). Not bypassed. Where the author's own arXiv copy exists it was read instead; Novelli, Taddeo and Floridi on accountability, Santoni de Sio and Mecacci on responsibility gaps, and Mantymaki et al. on defining organisational AI governance were not read and are not cited.

rejected.title: McNamara, Smith and Murphy-Hill, Does ACM's Code of Ethics Change Ethical Decision Making in Software Development? (ESEC/FSE 2018), author's copy
rejected.reason: Could not be reached (no response from the university server). The study is therefore cited only as reported in Hagendorff, and that is stated in the entry.

rejected.title: Jobin, Ienca and Vayena, Artificial Intelligence: the global landscape of ethics guidelines (arXiv 1906.11668)
rejected.reason: Abstract read. Maps the content of published principles; says less than Mittelstadt or Hagendorff about whether policies work inside an organisation. Not used.

rejected.title: ISO/IEC 42001 (AI policy clause)
rejected.reason: Not retried: recorded as HTTP 403 in the domain log on 2 October 2026. No claim is made about it.

brief_check: Nothing contradicts the brief. One addition it does not mention: the Divisional Court in Ayinde (6 June 2025, para 9) said leaders of legal practices must take practical and effective measures on AI use and that courts will ask whether they have. That is a sector-specific judicial expectation, not a general legal requirement, so 'No UK law requires an AI policy by name' stands.
